headline: Local Restaurant's 'Secret Menu' Revealed to Be Regular Menu Printed Upside Down
summary: Tony's Diner customers who 'knew to ask' received identical offerings at identical prices, rotated 180 degrees.
content:
For years, regulars at Tony's Diner have whispered about a "secret menu" available only to those who knew to ask for it. This week, first-time customer Melissa Chen discovered what long-time patrons had somehow missed: the secret menu is simply the regular menu, printed upside down.

"I asked the waiter about it because someone at work mentioned it," Chen recounted. "He got this very serious look, went to the back, and returned with what he called 'the real menu.' I turned it right-side up and it was literally the same menu. Same items. Same prices. Same little drawing of Tony giving a thumbs up."

Diner owner Tony Giordano, 63, confirmed that the "secret menu" has been a feature of the establishment since 1987.

"My father started it as a joke," Giordano explained. "Someone asked if we had a secret menu, and he was like, 'Sure,' and just flipped over a regular menu. People loved it. They felt like insiders. Who am I to take that away?"

The tradition has persisted for 37 years, with some customers reportedly ordering from the "secret menu" for decades without realizing the deception.

"I've been asking for the secret menu since the '90s," said regular customer Arthur Webb, 71, when informed of the truth. He was silent for a long moment. "Huh. I guess that explains why everything was always available."

Webb then ordered his usual—a club sandwich and coffee—from the upside-down menu he was handed.

"It still feels special," he said. "I'm going to choose to keep feeling special about it."

Giordano says he has no plans to discontinue the secret menu. "People want to feel like they're in on something," he said. "If an upside-down laminated piece of paper does that, who's it hurting?"
author: Ellen Park, Food & Dining
